object_description: four differently proportioned building cubes grouped around a square inner hall
geometry_property: mineral base with timber upper floors
design_condition: four cubes of different proportions are grouped around a square inner hall so that each responds spatially to the adjacent urban structure, with setbacks creating generous entrance squares

positive: The four cubes respond spatially in a differentiated manner to the adjacent urban structures
The tallest building answers the strong volume of the old town edge without crowding the listed house
Reducing the volume by one floor frames the street space opposite the historic suburban row
Setbacks create generous entrance squares connecting to the pedestrian routes
The setback creates the atmosphere of a wide boulevard opening like a square
Loose groups of trees zone this urban space
The consistent arrangement of food offerings creates a public character continuing the old town ambience
The cube on the opposite side gains an appropriate scale from the rising topography
The existing park-like hillside landscape is taken over and continued in high quality
The rear cube is staggered back one floor and transitions into the open structure of the adjoining district
Large representative entrances lead from all sides into the central four-storey hall
The ground floor expansion for entrance, foyer and sculptural spiral staircase characterises the public uses
It offers spacious lounge areas for the adjacent large rooms
Inner open work areas facing the hall are supplemented with pinwheel niches and loggias
These enable views of the urban space
The clear basic structure allows a variety of organisational forms for teaching and research
The functional divisions create the desired synergy between research and teaching
The height staggering creates open spaces on the upper floors assigned to teaching and work areas
These give different lounge areas in different garden designs, seen as positive
The disciplined structure with very compact plan promises construction costs in the lower range
The project is convincing overall in terms of the assessed sustainability
negative: The desired public character of the hall and the introverted upper floors cannot yet convince at this density
Considerable noise emissions can only be addressed through mechanical ventilation, inadequate for sound insulation
The material alienation citing historical public building motifs seems a bit too direct
It raises doubts about the desired expression of a university
The desired compactness with the publicity of the central hall is not yet convincing
Spatial and lighting quality and the usage arrangements of the upper floors are not convincing
